title: Chronic back pain + anterior vertebral destruction + paraspinal abscess in a TB-endemic immigrant: Pott disease (tuberculosis)
vignette: A 22-year-old man comes to the office due to 3 months of progressive back pain. He has also had intermittent subjective fever. The patient emigrated from Nepal for a master's program 6 months ago. He has no other medical conditions, takes no medication, and does not use tobacco, alcohol, or illicit drugs. Temperature is 38.3 C (100.9 F), blood pressure is 122/78 mm Hg, and pulse is 84/min. BMI is 19 kg/m2. Tenderness is noted over the lumbar spine; flexion, extension, and rotation of the spine are limited due to pain and muscle spasm. MRI of the lower spine reveals partial destruction of the anterior portion of the L1-L3 vertebral bodies and a fluid collection beneath the anterior longitudinal ligament. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

clues.note: Chronic back pain with low-grade constitutional fever suggests an indolent infectious/granulomatous process rather than a mechanical or neoplastic cause.
Nepal is a tuberculosis-endemic region; recent emigration is a strong clue for reactivation TB (including spinal TB).

clues.text: partial destruction of the anterior portion of the L1-L3 vertebral bodies and a fluid collection beneath the anterior longitudinal ligament
clues.note: Anterior vertebral body destruction with a paraspinal/subligamentous abscess is classic for TUBERCULOUS SPONDYLITIS (Pott disease).

whatMatters: Chronic progressive back pain + low-grade fever + ANTERIOR vertebral body destruction with a paraspinal (subligamentous) ABSCESS in a patient from a TB-endemic region = POTT DISEASE (Mycobacterium tuberculosis spondylitis), from hematogenous seeding/reactivation. Answer E.
strategy: Combine epidemiology (TB-endemic immigrant), tempo (months, constitutional fever), and imaging (anterior vertebral destruction + paraspinal abscess) -> tuberculous spondylitis. Reject: Hodgkin lymphoma (fever + adenopathy/mediastinal mass, not vertebral destruction with abscess), osteosarcoma (lytic bone tumor in long bones of young adults), rhabdomyosarcoma (soft-tissue sarcoma of head/neck/GU), and Staphylococcus aureus vertebral osteomyelitis/epidural abscess (usually IV drug use/bacteremia, more acute) - TB is favored by the endemic exposure and indolent course.

eliminations.label: Hodgkin lymphoma - adenopathy, not vertebral abscess
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: a lymphoma with fever (Pel-Ebstein), night sweats, and lymphadenopathy/mediastinal mass. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: vertebral body destruction with a paraspinal fluid collection is not typical; imaging/exam here fit an infectious process. ✅ Correct if: painless adenopathy with Reed-Sternberg cells.

eliminations.label: Osteosarcoma - lytic long-bone tumor
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: the most common primary bone tumor in young adults (metaphysis of long bones). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it affects long bones (e.g., distal femur) with a lytic/sunburst lesion, not anterior vertebral destruction with an abscess and fever. ✅ Correct if: a destructive long-bone lesion with Codman triangle.

eliminations.label: Rhabdomyosarcoma - soft-tissue sarcoma
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: a skeletal-muscle sarcoma of the head/neck or genitourinary tract. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it presents as a soft-tissue mass, not vertebral osteomyelitis with a subligamentous abscess and fever. ✅ Correct if: a soft-tissue mass (embryonal/alveolar histology).

eliminations.label: S aureus - more acute, IVDU/bacteremia
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: the most common cause of pyogenic vertebral osteomyelitis/spinal epidural abscess. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it is usually more ACUTE and arises with IV drug use, bacteremia, or spinal procedures; this indolent course in a TB-endemic immigrant favors Pott disease. ✅ Correct if: acute back pain with fever and IVDU/endocarditis source.

reasoning: Chronic progressive back pain with low-grade fever in a TB-endemic immigrant
MRI shows anterior vertebral body destruction with a paraspinal/subligamentous abscess
This pattern is classic for tuberculous spondylitis (Pott disease) from reactivation TB
mechanism: POTT DISEASE (tuberculous spondylitis) is Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection of the SPINE. Primary pulmonary TB is usually contained by the CELL-MEDIATED immune response, but transient BACTEREMIA can HEMATOGENOUSLY SEED highly vascular sites - including the VERTEBRAE (via Batson venous plexus) - where infection can REACTIVATE months to years later. Spinal TB classically destroys the ANTERIOR portions of adjacent VERTEBRAL BODIES and spreads BENEATH the anterior longitudinal ligament to involve neighboring vertebrae and the disc space, forming COLD (paraspinal/subligamentous) ABSCESSES and, in severe cases, vertebral collapse with kyphosis (gibbus deformity) and cord compression. It presents indolently with chronic back pain, low-grade fever, and constitutional symptoms - fitting this immigrant from a TB-endemic area. Diagnosis is supported by imaging and confirmed by biopsy/culture; treatment is prolonged multidrug anti-TB therapy. The distractors are lymphoma (adenopathy), osteosarcoma/rhabdomyosarcoma (tumors of long bones/soft tissue), and pyogenic (S aureus) osteomyelitis (more acute, IVDU/bacteremia).

difficulty.label: 🧠 Knowledge
difficulty.text: First Aid Micro/Ortho > Pott disease: M tuberculosis spinal infection; hematogenous seeding/reactivation; anterior vertebral body destruction + subligamentous (cold) abscess; kyphosis/gibbus; chronic back pain + constitutional symptoms; endemic-region exposure.

difficulty.label: 📖 Comprehension
difficulty.text: TB-endemic immigrant + chronic back pain + anterior vertebral destruction/abscess = Pott disease.

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
difficulty.text: Unsure on Pott disease, tuberculous spondylitis, hematogenous seeding, cold abscess, or gibbus deformity? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🨤 Distractor
difficulty.text: Hodgkin = adenopathy; osteosarcoma/rhabdomyosarcoma = long-bone/soft-tissue tumors; S aureus = acute pyogenic (IVDU).

difficulty.label: 🗒️ Other
difficulty.text: Bank: Pott disease = TB spondylitis (anterior vertebral destruction + paraspinal abscess) from reactivation; endemic exposure.
